numbers.what: pole length above the paving to the cap's top
numbers.source: a 3.0 m stop pole (the repository's research note and the 29 September script agree; P1's span flag top to foot gives 3.0 m only if the plate is 300 wide); error 150 mm

numbers.kind: Photo, scaled on the assumed width
numbers.source: P1: the white pole is 13 to 14 px wide on the 640 px copy (edges x 543.5 and 556.5 at rows 200 to 225; 543.5 and 557.5 at rows 395 to 410; my own edge finder gives 544.1 and 557.5), 13.5 px x 6.56 mm per px = 89 mm: a 3 1/2 inch (89 mm) tube; against the flag's 45.7 px that is 0.30 (+-0.03) while the first version built 76 / 300 = 0.25 (it had read the pole as 7 to 8 px = 50 mm and kept the 76 mm standard). The scale rests on the assumed plate width (N3)

assumed 300 mm: it sets P1's scale (6.56 mm per px); P1 flag_left 526.0 to flag_right 571.7 = 45.7 px. The photograph fixes only the RATIO of the pole to the plate: with a 76 mm pole the plate would be about 255 mm, outside this number's old +-30, so the source error is +-50 (a stop plate is 250 to 350 wide); N2, N4 to N7 and N10 are scaled on it

photos.method: each edge is the strongest grey-level step inside the recorded window, averaged over the recorded band; the scale is fitted on the one span from the flag plate's top edge to the case's lower edge (303.6 px); the plate's width is the unit that sets 6.56 mm per px (Judgement), so the absolute sizes are judged within the stated errors and the photograph checks the proportions; case sides were too faint to measure; the band-2 foot (the white band's lower end) has a spread of 3.6 px; the tolerance is the measured spread times 3 plus 2 px, at least 5 px (33 mm)

sources.author: Jaggery
sources.shows: an old-style bus stop in a Cotswold village: an enamel flag with BUS STOP in two lines on a black pole with white bands, a dark-green timetable case with a clear window (blank upper half, a paper card in the lower half) clamped below the flag; the foot is in shadow

placement.slot: west pavement, pole centre at x 46.0 m (the cast's bus stop, hook-cast.json), 0.50 m behind the kerb's back edge (z -3.625), the flag and the case facing -x (south, towards the bus coming up the street); the waiting spot z -4.3 is behind it; no shelter
reasons: the cast already puts the stop at x 46.0, z -4.3 on the west pavement (production/specs/hook-cast.json: 'the bus stop at the top of Quay Street'), and the west row's newsagent (west_north, x 36 to 42) lies below it (Rita's is on the east side, across the street); the scene file has no stop, so this is a new slot (the 29 September README said the street had none)
a bus on the west lane travels north (+x) with the kerb on its left; the flag must face the bus coming from the south, so it faces -x; waiting people read the case from the road side of the pole

no shelter: a shelter is 1.2 to 1.5 m deep and would leave 0.5 to 0.8 m of a 2.0 m footway, under the 1.0 m this target requires behind a pole (the tester's walk found 0.65 m too narrow on 29 September); the stop is a pole with a case
the litter bin B3 of the litter-bins target (the hooded drum K2) stands at x 44.0 west, z -3.8, 2.0 m from the pole, inside the 3 m the asset plan asks for
the stop is beyond the west row's end (west_north runs to x 42; the stop is 4.0 m past it), so no shopfront is hidden by the pole or the queue

wear: the pole's paint is chipped to grey primer within 300 mm of the paving (kicks, bicycle pedals); the lowest 120 mm has a dark splash line; the white band is street-grey
scraps of old sticker and tape on the pole between 1.2 and 1.6 m, never legible; a few dog marks at the foot (nothing else at the foot)

the flag plate: chips at the bolt holes with rust runs 30 to 80 mm long, a bent corner, a patch of yellow-green lichen and bird lime along its lower edge and clamp (P1 shows yellow lichen under the plate), the plate off square by 2 to 3 degrees (the sample's lean; BS1 is built square and the lean is a seed)

the case: green faded to grey-green on its top bar, a dirt line along the window's lower edge, two fine scratches on the sheet, one cracked corner of the sheet in the worn variant, the card yellowed at the edges with its top corner curled
NOT shown: any advertisement on the case, any person, any drink, any real operator's logo

variants_note: BS1 (the sample): pole, old-style flag, timetable case. One on the street.
BS2: pole and flag only (no case), the same pole and flag: for a second stop if the town wants one (none today).
conditions (materials): C0 sound; C1 worn (the sample's wear); C2 flag knocked 3 degrees off square with a bent corner and a cracked case sheet (a seed, not a mesh).
timetable cards: T1 as written; T2 the same card yellowed with a curled corner and one service struck through in ink (a mask over T1, never other times).
not_settled: absolute sizes: S1 has no scale object, the plate's width (300 mm) is assumed and sets 6.56 mm per px; every size from S1 is Judgement within the stated error (the flag's height, the case's height and its height above the paving, the white band's lower end)
the case's width and depth (the sides were too faint to measure; 260 wide and 60 deep are typical)
the 1990 flag type on the real street (S1's old enamel plate or the pictogram plate of S3): either is period; S1 is chosen because a photograph exists
the real timetable's look (S2 is 2010 and carries an operator's logo, so only its stacking of text blocks is used)
whether Quay Street's stop had a shelter in the cast's mind (the cast gives only the stop)
content_rule_note: no advertisement, no person, no drink or betting wording on the case or card (a statement of the content rule).
builder_notes: pole: three tubes (black, white, black) of 76 mm and a cap; the paving collar is a short cylinder; weld the three tubes into one mesh with one material id each

flag plate: 3 mm with corners r 20 and the edge rolled back 4 mm; the border and the two lines of capitals are texture on the plate, not meshes; the border strips in the parts table are the raised edge's guide (2 mm)
case: four folded bars (60 deep), a 6 mm back sheet, a 2 mm clear sheet, the card 4 px per mm (800 x 1880 px) with the text from text.services set in the stated font; the card has no logo
orientation: the local -y faces the bus (towards -x in the street's frame, yaw 90 degrees)
